'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]], [[Battle of Kandahar (2021)]]
****The [[Taliban]] captures the [[Provinces of Afghanistan|provincial]] capitals of [[Ghazni]], [[Qala e Naw]], [[Kandahar]] and [[Herat]], bringing the number of provincial capitals taken in the past seven days to thirteen. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/taliban-battle-government-forces-us-fears-kabul-could-fall-90-days-2021-08-12/ (Reuters)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/12/afghanistan-taliban-kandahar-prison-police-ghazni-live-updates (Al Jazeera)] [https://apnews.com/article/middle-east-afghanistan-taliban-26d485963b7a0d9f2107afcbc38f239a (Associated Press)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/08/12/world/asia/kandahar-afghanistan-taliban.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)|Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan]]
***[[The Pentagon]] announces it will send [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. troops]] to [[Kabul]]'s [[Hamid Karzai International Airport]] to help [[Operation Allies Refuge|evacuate]] staff from the [[Embassy of the United States, Kabul|U.S. Embassy]] while [[Spokesperson for the United States Department of State|U.S. Department of State spokesperson]] [[Ned Price]] states that the embassy will remain open. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/u-s-expected-to-significantly-cut-personnel-from-kabul-embassy-11628790834 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
**The [[Government of the United Kingdom|British government]] announces that 600 [[British Armed Forces|troops]] will be [[Military deployment|deployed]] to Afghanistan on a short-term basis in order to help evacuate British citizens and protect Afghan staff and [[interpreter]]s. Around 4,000 UK nationals are currently in the country. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-58195286 (BBC News)]
**[[Government of Afghanistan|Afghan authorities]] arrest Dawood Laghmani, the [[List of governors of Ghazni|governor of Ghazni province]], for abandoning the [[Ghazni city|city of Ghazni]] when the Taliban captured it. The [[Ministry of Interior Affairs (Afghanistan)|Interior Ministry]] also reports the arrest of many of Laghmani's colleagues. [https://www.aninews.in/news/world/asia/afghan-security-forces-arrest-ghazni-governor-dawood-laghmani-interior-ministry20210812165433/ (Asian News International)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**The [[Tigray Defense Forces]] seize the city of [[Weldiya]] in the [[Amhara Region]] as they continue to advance south. [https://foreignpolicy.com/2021/08/11/abiy-tigray-tplf-ethiopia/ (''Foreign Policy'')]
*[[Plymouth shooting]]
**Six people, including the gunman, are killed and two more are wounded in a [[mass shooting]] in [[Plymouth]], [[Devon]], [[England]]. Eyewitnesses say that the shooting began at a house before the shooter "randomly started shooting" on the street. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-devon-58195419 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A helicopter carrying 13 [[tourism in Russia|tourists]] and three crew members crashes into [[Kurile Lake]] in [[Kamchatka Krai]], [[Russia]]. Eight of the people on board survived, while the fate of the others remain unknown. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-58182420 (BBC News)]
*[[Flash flood|Flash flooding]] in [[Turkey]]'s northern [[Kastamonu Province]] kills nine people, while flooding in the [[Sinop Province]] leaves one person missing. Four bridges have collapsed and 170 villages are without power while over 900 people have been evacuated, according to a statement from the [[Disaster and Emergency Management Presidency]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/flash-floods-northern-turkey-kill-four-one-missing-2021-08-12/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia]]
*****[[British Columbia]] announces that everyone working in long-term care and seniors’ [[assisted living]] facilities will be [[Vaccine mandate|required to be vaccinated]] against [[COVID-19]] by mid-October, becoming the first [[Provinces of Canada|province in Canada]] to impose such a mandate. [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/amp/canada/british-columbia/article-british-columbia-makes-covid-19-vaccines-mandatory-for-long-term-care/ (''The Globe and Mail'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
*****[[COVID-19 pandemic in the San Francisco Bay Area]]
******[[Mayor of San Francisco|San Francisco mayor]] [[London Breed]] issues a mandate requiring proof of full vaccination in indoor public spaces, making [[San Francisco]] the first [[Lists of cities in the United States|major U.S. city]] to do so. [https://www.ktvu.com/news/san-francisco-to-become-1st-major-city-to-require-full-vaccination-restaurants-gyms (KTVU)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Missouri]]
*****[[Missouri]] surpasses 10,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://fox2now.com/news/missouri/missouris-covid-death-toll-surpasses-10000/ (KTVI)]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
*****[[United States Secretary of Health and Human Services|U.S. Health Secretary]] [[Xavier Becerra]] announces that the [[United States Department of Health and Human Services|U.S. Department of Health and Human Services]] will [[COVID-19 vaccine mandates in the United States|require]] healthcare workers to receive a [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.politico.com/news/2021/08/12/hhs-mandates-covid-19-vaccinations-for-health-care-workforce-504138 (''Politico'')]
*****The [[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. Food and Drug Administration]] authorizes a [[booster dose]] of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] and [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna]] COVID-19 vaccines for [[immunocompromise|immunocompromised]] people. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-fda-authorizes-covid-19-vaccine-boosters-immunocompromised-2021-08-13/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Cambodia]] begins to administer the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]] as a third "booster" dose to people who have received the inactivated virus vaccines developed by [[Sinopharm]] ([[BBIBP-CorV]]) and [[Sinovac]] ([[CoronaVac]]) in order to strengthen immunity against the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]]. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/paper/2021/08/12/cambodia-starts-vaccine-booster-drive-to-shore-up-covid-19-defense.html (''The Jakarta Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 18,822 new cases of COVID-19. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/08/12/national/coronavirus-cases-august-12/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 21,688 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,342,215. [https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2021/08/12/record-high-21668-covid-19-cases/?__cf_chl_jschl_tk__=pmd_1b43a37331311507a4fe050075996c87c3d94c68-1628770690-0-gqNtZGzNAmKjcnBszQcO (''Free Malaysia Today'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 22,782 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 839,771. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1472596/thailand-reports-record-22782-coronavirus-cases (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] opens registration for children between the ages of 12 and 15 to receive a COVID-19 vaccine. Around 280,000 children will be eligible for vaccination with the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] or [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna]] vaccines, with more than 50,000 already registered. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-58184278 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 808 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 168,049. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/08/12/russia-sets-new-pandemic-record-with-over-800-coronavirus-deaths-a74767 (''The Moscow Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Australian Capital Territory]]
****The [[Australian Capital Territory]] enters a [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] after the first locally acquired case of COVID-19 in over a year was reported. Every [[State and territory of Australia|state and territory]] on the [[Eastern states of Australia|east coast of Australia]], where the majority of the national population lives, is now under a lockdown. The last time this occurred was at the beginning of the pandemic in 2020. [https://www.theaustralian.com.au/breaking-news/canberra-expected-to-enter-a-lockdown-due-to-a-case-of-covid19-in-act/news-story/f59ccdea9eb84081f741d0012612832f (''The Australian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Lesotho]]
***[[Lesotho]] [[Prime Minister of Lesotho|prime minister]] [[Moeketsi Majoro]] self-isolates after [[COVID-19 testing|testing]] positive for COVID-19. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2021/aug/12/lesothos-pm-isolating-with-covid-as-cases-go-unrecorded (''The Guardian'')]
**The [[Moderna]] COVID-19 vaccine is found to be effective against the [[SARS-CoV-2 lineage B.1.617|Lineage B.1.617]] [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]] for six months. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/08/12/health/moderna-vaccine-protection/index.html (CNN)]
*The population of [[white Americans]] declines for [[Demographic history of the United States|the first time]], and [[population growth]] is at its lowest since the [[Great Depression]], per the results of the [[2020 United States census|2020 census]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-release-census-data-used-legislative-redistricting-2021-08-12/ (Reuters)]
'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of Vanuatu]]
**[[Vanuatu]] stops the sale of its [[citizenship]] and revokes the citizenship it gave last April to a [[Syrian diaspora|Syrian national]] for US$130,000. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/449063/vanuatu-sells-citizenship-in-april-takes-it-away-in-august (RNZ International)]
*[[Foreign relations of Argentina]], [[AMIA bombing]], [[Iran and state-sponsored terrorism]]
**[[Argentina]] condemns the designation of [[Ahmad Vahidi]] to a [[Ministry of Interior (Iran)|ministerial rank]] in the [[Government of Ebrahim Raisi|new government]] of [[President of Iran|President]] [[Ebrahim Raisi]] in [[Iran]]. Argentina issued a [[Interpol notice|red notice]] through [[INTERPOL]] against Vahidi for his alleged connection with the 1994 [[AMIA bombing]]. The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Worship|Foreign Ministry]] expressed its condemnation of the designation as "an affront to the [[Argentine law|Argentine justice]] and the victims of the [[Terrorism in Argentina|brutal terrorist attack]]". [https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/argentina/argentina-condemns-appointment-of-iranian-minister-linked-to-amia-attack.phtml (''Buenos Aires Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Turkey's migrant crisis]]
**Armed locals in [[Ankara]], [[Turkey]], attack shops, houses and cars owned by [[Syrians in Turkey|Syrians]]. The assaults occurred after a Turkish teenager was killed yesterday during [[Racism in Turkey|a fight between Syrians and locals]], and the wounding of Turkish men who were stabbed by a Syrian man in another incident. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-58185612 (BBC News)]
*[[2021 Algeria wildfires]]
**[[President of Algeria|President]] [[Abdelmadjid Tebboune]], in a televised address, announces that 22 people have been arrested for causing the wildfires which have left 65 people dead so far. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/algeria-leader-calls-wildfires-disaster-says-22-arsonists-arrested-2021-08-12/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Political impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[2021 Madagascar food crisis]]
**[[List of presidents of Madagascar|President]] [[Andry Rajoelina]] dismisses his entire [[Government of Madagascar|cabinet]] citing "failures in government" as the country struggles with severe [[Famine|food shortages]], an [[COVID-19 pandemic in Madagascar|increasing number of COVID-19 infections]] and a [[political crisis]] over a recently uncovered plot to assassinate [[President of Madagascar|the president]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20210812-madagascar-president-sacks-all-his-ministers-citing-failures-in-government (France 24)]
